oscillate: To swing back and forth, especially if with a regular rhythm.
oscillated: simple past and past participle of oscillate
oscillates: third-person singular simple present indicative of oscillate
oscillating: Moving in a repeated back-and-forth motion; coming and going.
oscillation: the act of oscillating or the state of being oscillated
oscillator: A tuned electronic circuit used to generate a continuous output waveform.
oscillogram: A record produced by an oscillograph or oscilloscope.
oscillograph: An instrument for measuring alternating or varying electric current in terms of current and voltage; an oscilloscope.
oscillographic: Of or pertaining to an oscillograph
oscillography: Measurement by means of an oscillograph.
oscilloscope: An electronic measuring instrument that creates a visible two-dimensional graph, on a screen, of one or more continuously varying voltages or currents.
oscilloscopic: Relating to, or carried out by using an oscilloscope.
oscine: Of or pertaining to songbirds (suborder Passeri).
oscinine: Of or pertaining to the Oscines, or songbirds (birds of the clade Passeri).
osculant: Adhering closely; applied to certain creeping animals, such as caterpillars.
oscular: Of or pertaining to the mouth.
osculated: simple past and past participle of osculate
osculates: third-person singular simple present indicative of osculate
osculating: present participle and gerund of osculate
osculatory: A religious tablet, usually carrying a representation of Christ or the Virgin Mary, which is kissed by the priest during the Mass ("kiss of peace"); it is then passed to others…
oses: The various sugars ending in -ose, such as sucrose, lactose, glucose, and fructose.
osier: A willow, of species Salix viminalis, growing in wet places in Europe and Asia, and introduced into North America, considered the best willow for wickerwork.
osmatic: Relating to the sense of smell.
osmeterium: One of a pair of scent organs in the larvae of certain swallowtail butterflies.
osmic: Pertaining to, derived from, or containing, osmium; specifically, designating those compounds in which it has a higher valence.
osmious: Denoting those compounds of osmium in which the element has a valence relatively lower than in the osmic compounds.
osmiridium: A hard, corrosion-resistant alloy of osmium and iridium, used in pen nibs.
osmium: A chemical element (symbol Os) with atomic number 76: a hard, brittle, heavy, bluish-white transition metal found as a trace element in alloys, mostly in platinum ores.
osmolality: The molality of an ideal solution that would exert the same osmotic pressure as the solution being considered.
osmolarity: The osmotic concentration of a solution, normally expressed as osmoles of solute per litre of solution.
osmole: A unit of measurement, a mole of an osmotically active compound
osmometer: Any of various devices used to measure osmotic pressure.
osmoregulation: The homeostatic regulation of osmotic pressure in the body in order to maintain a certain water content (concentration of electrolytes, pH, etc).
osmosed: simple past and past participle of osmose
osmosing: present participle and gerund of osmose
osmosis: The net movement of solvent molecules, usually water, from a region of lower solute concentration to a region of higher solute concentration through a partially permeable membrane.
osmotic: Relating to, or powered by, osmosis.
osmund: Alternative form of osmunda (“type of fern”).
osmunda: A fern of the genus Osmunda, especially the royal fern, Osmunda regalis.
osnaburg: A plain, coarse textile fabric made from flax, tow or jute yarns.
osprey: A bird of prey of genus Pandion that feeds on fish and has white underparts and long, narrow wings each ending in four finger-like extensions.
osseous: Of, relating to, or made of bone; bony.
ossia: In a musical score, an alternative version of a passage, usually just a few measures long.
ossicle: A small bone (or bony structure), especially one of the three of the middle ear.
ossicular: Related to or composed of ossicles.
ossific: Capable of producing bone; having the power to change cartilage or other tissue into bone.
ossification: The normal process by which bone is formed.
ossified: Having undergone the process of ossification (transformation into bone or a bone-like mass).
ossifier: One who, or that which, ossifies.
ossifies: third-person singular simple present indicative of ossify
ossifrage: Gypaetus barbatus, the bearded vulture, the diet of which is almost exclusively bone marrow.
ossify: To transform (or cause to transform) from a softer animal substance into bone; particularly the processes of growth in humans and animals.
ossifying: present participle and gerund of ossify
ossuary: A container, receptacle, or building, such as an urn or vault, for holding the bones of the dead.
ostensible: Apparent, evident; meant for open display.
ostensibly: Seemingly, apparently, on the surface; supposedly, according to representations or implications made by someone (especially when their motives are suspected by others).
ostensive: Apparently true, but not necessarily; ostensible
ostentation: Ambitious display; vain show; display intended to excite admiration or applause.
ostentatiously: In an ostentatious manner; extravagantly or flamboyantly.
ostentatiousness: The property or characteristic of being ostentatious.
osteoarthritis: A form of arthritis, affecting mainly older people, caused by chronic degeneration of the cartilage and synovial membrane of the joints, leading to pain and stiffness.
osteoblast: A mononucleate cell from which bone develops.
osteoblastic: Of or pertaining to an osteoblast
osteoclast: A large multinuclear cell associated with the resorption of bone.
osteoclastic: Of or pertaining to an osteoclast
osteocyte: A mature bone cell involved with the maintenance of bone.
osteogenesis: The formation and development of bone.
osteoid: Of, pertaining to, or characteristic of bone; bonelike
osteologist: A scientist or physician whose speciality is osteology.
osteology: The scientific study of the morphology and pathology of bones.
osteoma: A benign bony tumour that typically grows on the skull.
osteomalacia: A softening of adult bones due to inadequate mineralization; the adult equivalent of rickets.
osteopath: A non-physician healthcare practitioner who practices osteopathy by manipulating the skeleton and muscles.
osteopathic: of or pertaining to osteopathy or osteopathic medicine
osteopathy: The branch of therapy based on manipulation of bones and muscles.
osteoplasty: Surgery to repair, modify or graft bone or bony structures.
osteoporosis: A disease, occurring especially in women following menopause, in which the bones become extremely porous and are subject to fracture.
osteosarcoma: A type of cancer of the bone.
ostiary: The mouth of a river; an estuary.
ostinato: A piece of melody, a chord progression, or a bass figure that is repeated over and over as a musical accompaniment.
ostiolar: Of or pertaining to the ostiole.
ostiole: A small hole or opening through which certain fungi release their mature spores.
ostium: A small opening or orifice, as in a body organ or passage.
ostler: A person employed at an inn, hostelry, or stable to look after horses; a groom.
ostmark: The currency unit of the former German Democratic Republic (aka GDR, DDR, East Germany) until 1990, abbreviated DDM.
ostomy: A surgical procedure to provide an exit point for the waste of an organism.
ostracise: Non-Oxford British English standard spelling of ostracize.
ostracised: simple past and past participle of ostracise
ostracises: third-person singular simple present indicative of ostracise
ostracising: present participle and gerund of ostracise
ostracism: In ancient Athens (and some other cities), the temporary banishment by popular vote of a citizen considered dangerous to the state.
ostracize: To ban a person from a city for five or ten years through the procedure of ostracism.
ostracized: simple past and past participle of ostracize
ostracizes: third-person singular simple present indicative of ostracize
ostracizing: present participle and gerund of ostracize
ostracod: Any of many small crustaceans, of the class Ostracoda, that resemble a shrimp enclosed in a bivalve shell.
ostracoderm: Any of the armored jawless fishes of the Paleozoic.
ostracon: A piece of pottery or stone, usually broken off from a vase or other earthenware vessel, especially one used to cast a vote during the Ancient Greek process of ostracism.
ostrich: A large flightless bird of the order Struthioniformes.
ostrichlike: Resembling or characteristic of an ostrich; struthian
